transcript:
Date: 2026-03-14
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Carlos Reyes (Redwood SE); Leah Wong (Redwood Solutions); Rajesh Iyer (AuroraCloud - Head of Partnerships); Sophie Marc (AuroraCloud - Marketplace PM); Tom Becker (AuroraCloud - Cloud Integrations Lead); Ellen Price (AuroraCloud - Security Eng)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. Quick roll call? 
[00:07] Rajesh Iyer: Yep, Rajesh here. Sophie, Tom, Ellen on our side. 
[00:12] Carlos Reyes: Carlos from Redwood, here. I'll be driving the technical bits. 
[00:18] Sophie Marc: Sophie - great to meet you all. 
[00:25] Maya Patel: Awesome. Goal for today is to align on the marketplace listing requirements, walk through a proposed reference architecture for a joint solution (hosted + private option), and define a POC scope. Does that sound right? 
[00:34] Tom Becker: Yes that's right, and we want to make sure we understand what assets you need from us and what security artefacts will be necessary for AuroraCloud to list on the marketplace. 
[00:45] Maya Patel: Perfect. I'll share screen with the RA draft in a sec. Carlos, want to kick off with the deployment model options? 
[00:52] Carlos Reyes: Sure. So from Redwood side we usually recommend two patterns for marketplace integrations. One is a hosted listing where customers can purchase via Aurora marketplace and we serve from Redwood hosted API; second is a private/managed deployment where we provide a private control plane and the model runtime runs in customer or Aurora-managed infra — that one needs VPC peering, KMS integration, and some extra audit hooks. 
[01:20] Ellen Price: Quick Q — for the hosted option, how do you handle customer data residency and KMS? We have strict keys policy; we prefer not to have plaintext logs leave our VPC. 
[01:33] Carlos Reyes: Good question. Hosted mode can support envelope encryption and customer-owned keys via bring-your-own-KMS through our marketplace integration; however some customers with strict requirements opt for the private deployment where keys never leave the VPC. There's some tradeoff with latency and cost. 
[01:52] Sophie Marc: For Aurora marketplace, we also have a requirement for a 'supported regions' list and a compliance pack (SOC2 summary, privacy policy, sample SLA). Do you have a standard checklist? 
[02:05] Maya Patel: Yes we have a marketplace onboarding doc — we'll share the checklist after the call. It includes supported regions, security docs, and example assets (logos, screenshots, 1-pager). Also we usually ask for a small demo script for the listing page. 
[02:20] Rajesh Iyer: On the reference arch, can you show how billing and metering will flow? We need to ensure marketplace can capture usage to bill customers correctly. 
[02:29] Leah Wong: Absolutely. In the RA draft we propose a metering hook: Redwood emits per-customer usage events to a secure webhook endpoint that Aurora marketplace ingests; alternatively, for private deployments, Aurora can call an API to retrieve aggregated usage statements. We'll share the spec. 
[02:50] Tom Becker: Does that require us to open inbound endpoints to your systems? We're cautious about that. 
[02:57] Carlos Reyes: Not necessarily; we can push usage events to a pre-configured Aurora endpoint over TLS, authenticated by mTLS or a signed JWT. For private deployments you can export metrics via Prometheus scraping or a push gateway into Aurora billing. 
[03:18] Sophie Marc: About SSO, we use SAML for our marketplace admin portal, and we need partners to support Just-in-Time provisioning. How do you integrate with SSO? 
[03:28] Carlos Reyes: We support SAML and OIDC; JIT provisioning is supported for SAML with attribute mapping. For Private instances, you can integrate via customer IdP using SAML and Redwood supports SCIM for provisioning. We'll need example SAML metadata from your side. 
[03:45] Ellen Price: Are there any constraints with our HSM? We use a cloud HSM for key custody and rotate keys monthly. 
[03:52] Carlos Reyes: We integrate with cloud KMS offerings and can support HSM-backed keys; rotation is supported, though note we need aligned rotation windows for cache warmup/EVP re-keys. We'll put recommended rotation windows in the KMS notes. 
[04:08] Rajesh Iyer: Can we talk about the RA topology? 
[04:11] Maya Patel: (screen share) Here's the draft reference architecture: top left is Aurora marketplace, top right is Redwood control plane, bottom is runtime clusters. For hosted listing, customers authenticate via marketplace and we provision a tenant in Redwood, with metrics and audit logs pushed to Aurora. For private, we show a connector and VPC peering with an optional sidecar for logs and metrics. 
[04:40] Tom Becker: The diagram shows a 'connector' that needs network egress. Can the connector live in our subnet? 
[04:47] Carlos Reyes: Yes, the connector can be deployed within your subnet; it requires outbound TLS to Redwood control plane endpoints. Port requirements are minimal (443) and we support proxying through your egress. 
[05:02] Sophie Marc: For the marketplace listing we'll need a sandbox account to validate the provisioning flow. Can we get a test tenant? 
[05:10] Maya Patel: Absolutely. We'll provision a sandbox tenant and seed it with a small test quota. 
[05:18] Rajesh Iyer: On the legal side, our procurement team will want the data processing addendum and indemnities. How have you handled this with other marketplaces? 
[05:28] Maya Patel: We have a standard DPA and marketplace addendum; I'll have legal send the template to Rajesh's team. 
[05:36] Rajesh Iyer: Great. 
[05:40] Leah Wong: Any constraints on model variants? If a customer wants quantized models for cost, does the marketplace listing need to enumerate those? 
[05:49] Carlos Reyes: We usually include model variants in the listing metadata (e.g., base model, 8-bit quantized variant, latency profile). That helps marketplace filter by performance/cost. 
[06:02] Tom Becker: For the POC, our engineering lead wants to validate end-to-end provisioning and SSO flows plus an on-prem private deployment smoke test. Can we scope that? 
[06:12] Maya Patel: Yes, propose a 6-week POC: week 1 onboarding & asset handoff; week 2 sandbox provisioning and listing validation; week 3 SSO/KMS integration; week 4 private connector deployment; week 5 performance benchmarks; week 6 wrap and next steps. 
[06:30] Rajesh Iyer: That timeline seems doable, aligns with our Q2 goals. Budget approval pending. 
[06:40] Sophie Marc: One more question — monitoring & support: we need 24/7 escalation path for production issues from marketplace customers. How does Redwood handle PagerDuty and SLAs? 
[06:51] Maya Patel: For marketplace customers on hosted mode we offer email support; for marketplace-integrated enterprise customers we can map through a dedicated support tier and integrate your PagerDuty via webhook. SLAs can be negotiated depending on Dedicated/private commitments. 
[07:07] Ellen Price: Do you have SOC2 report we can share with auditors? 
[07:12] Maya Patel: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II; I'll attach the summary and contact our security team for full reports under NDA if needed. 
[07:20] Tom Becker: Regarding networking, do you support IPv6? Some of our regions require it. 
[07:26] Carlos Reyes: We support IPv6 for control plane endpoints; for runtime clusters it depends on the provider. We'll confirm and add to action items. 
[07:38] Rajesh Iyer: Any concerns about multi-tenant performance if we run many marketplace tenants in a region? 
[07:45] Leah Wong: Our runtime supports reserved capacity pools for marketplace customers; we can propose dedicated capacity options for Aurora marketplace launch partners to guarantee latency. 
[07:58] Sophie Marc: For listing assets, format requirements for screenshots, logos? 
[08:03] Maya Patel: We'll send a checklist; typically PNG logo 1024x1024, a 1-pager PDF, 3 screenshots 1200x800. 
[08:15] Rajesh Iyer: On security, we'll need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Is that available? 
[08:21] Carlos Reyes: Yes, audit logs can be shipped via secure syslog or S3 export; also we support event streaming to your Kafka or webhook. We'll include formats. 
[08:35] Tom Becker: Great. About the RA diagram, can Redwood annotate the diagram with recommended firewall rules and IAM roles? 
[08:43] Leah Wong: Yes we'll add a layer with suggested Security Groups, least-privilege IAM roles, and required API scopes. 
[08:50] Sophie Marc: Anything we should be aware of from the legal/inventory side for marketplace policies? 
[08:55] Rajesh Iyer: We'll need to ensure compliance with our marketplace content policies — nothing misleading and proper data handling language. Sophie will follow up. 
[09:05] Maya Patel: Quick recap and next steps — we'll (1) share the RA diagram, (2) send marketplace checklist and asset templates, (3) provision sandbox tenant, (4) legal will share DPA template, (5) schedule SSO/KMS deep dive with Ellen and Carlos. Any other items? 
[09:22] Tom Becker: Please include the sample network egress rules. 
[09:26] Carlos Reyes: Will do. 
[09:28] Rajesh Iyer: Let's plan the SSO/KMS deep dive for next week, aim for Wed. 
[09:33] Maya Patel: Sounds good; I'll send calendar invites. Thanks everyone. 
[09:38] Sophie Marc: Thanks all. 

End transcript.
